title: Na autobus
reviewerNotes: This full draft is ready for human review before publication.
storyBeat: Ana and Emir buy bus tickets and dream of Jablanica lake views and Neum on the coast.

vocabulary: Buy a bus ticket with karta, stanica, and price phrases.
Name seat, window, driver, departure, and arrival words.
Talk about a coast trip toward Neum.
grammar: Use Treba mi and trebaš to say what you need.
Ask Koliko košta karta? then choose jednosmjerna or povratna.
Read odlazak and dolazak on a station board.
culture: Start from the Sarajevo bus station toward lake and coast.
Picture Jablaničko Lake on the southbound road.
Notice how road corridors and entity borders affect travel.

grammar.title: Treba mi and trebaš
grammar.explanation: Treba mi means I need, and the thing you need comes right after it. Trebaš means you need, for one person you know well. Keep the phrase together and stay in the present tense.

grammar.title: Ticket questions at the counter
grammar.explanation: Ask Koliko košta karta? to find the price. Add jednosmjerna or povratna before karta to choose one-way or return. Finish with molim when you speak to the clerk.

examples.english: How much does the ticket cost?

grammar.title: Station timing chunks
grammar.explanation: Say the whole line together. Skip the full chart for now. Use odlazak for departure and dolazak for arrival. Pair each word with a clock time you already know. These present-tense lines help you read a board without learning a new tense.

culture.title: From the station toward lake and coast
culture.body: Sarajevo's main bus station sends coaches and minibuses toward the lakes and the coast. Ana buys a ticket while Emir shows her a postcard of Jablaničko Lake, the blue water you pass on the road south. What they really want is Neum, the short stretch of Adriatic coast that gives Bosnia and Herzegovina a seaside town. From a window seat, they picture the sea air waiting after the mountain tunnels. The departure board lists odlazak times while travelers wait nearby with coffee and bags. A few ticket phrases turn a daydream about the coast into an actual trip.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson A. Ticket counter phrases
lessonBlocks.body: Start with autobus, karta, and stanica so the station feels familiar before you even reach the doors. Add vozač, sjedalo, and prozor for concrete nouns you can point to on the ride. Practice Treba mi karta until it sounds automatic at a busy counter, then ask Koliko košta karta? and choose jednosmjerna or povratna before you pay. Ana stands at the Sarajevo counter with Emir, already picturing the lake stop near Jablanica. You don't need every case ending to buy a ticket, just these few working lines. Try each counter line a couple of times, then look at the board and name odlazak or dolazak in a full sentence.
tips: Keep Treba mi and the noun together as one phrase.
Add molim when you speak to the ticket clerk.
Choose jednosmjerna or povratna before you pay.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson B. Board and dream of Neum
lessonBlocks.body: Move from the counter to your seat once the ticket is in your hand. Say Imam sjedalo uz prozor when you claim a window seat for the lake view later. Reuse Molim and Hvala with the clerk, then tell a friend Trebaš kartu before the doors close. Ana wants Neum, Emir wants the lake view, and Mrvica stays home with Amira for the day. Stay in the present tense. You can buy and board today without touching past or future forms. Chain the pieces together out loud: need, price, ticket type, seat, thank you, and one calm boarding line. Run through the chain a few times until boarding feels easy.
tips: Reuse Hvala after you receive the ticket.
Practice sjedalo uz prozor before you sit.
Stay in present tense even when you talk about the coast dream.

funFacts.title: Neum is the short coast
funFacts.body: Neum is the Adriatic town that gives Bosnia and Herzegovina a coastline. The stretch is short compared with neighboring countries, but it still has beaches and good seafood. Most travelers reach it by road from inland cities. The coast dream in this lesson is a real destination, not just a postcard fantasy.

funFacts.title: Jablanica sits on the lake road
funFacts.body: Jablaničko Lake appears on many southbound routes from Sarajevo. The water sits in a mountain corridor and often becomes a rest stop in travelers' stories. Emir's postcard keeps the lake in view while Ana buys tickets. It's a reminder that the trip to the coast includes some inland beauty too.

funFacts.title: Treba mi is a survival phrase
funFacts.body: Treba mi plus a noun is one of the fastest ways to name what you need at a counter. You don't need a full conjugation table to buy a ticket. Pair it with molim and you'll sound ready for any clerk. Simple present-tense phrases like this keep Book 1 practical.

funFacts.title: Window seats teach prozor
funFacts.body: Sjedalo uz prozor turns furniture words into travel comfort. You already know a few short location phrases, and a window seat makes them stick. Ana picks hers for the view toward the lake and coast. Suddenly vocabulary practice comes with real scenery.

civicContext.title: Corridor Vc still leaves the country half connected
civicContext.body: Buying a bus ticket in Bosnia and Herzegovina means traveling on a map that is still unfinished. The EU-backed Corridor Vc motorway is meant to run north to south through the country, yet only part of it is open after years of loans, delays, and political fights over routes. Other motorway projects, serving Banja Luka and the southern border approaches toward Međugorje and Croatia, have moved forward on their own separate timelines. A coach toward the coast can still pass long gaps where a modern national highway was promised and never delivered.
